Sqlite.Auth.Password.name: Sqlite.Auth.Password
Sqlite.Auth.Password.comment:
Set, check, change, and reset users' passwords.

## Expected database schema

This module owns two tables. The minimum required schema for each is below.

### Passwords table

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS passwords (
        user_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        password TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        last_used INTEGER,
        failed_login_attempts_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (failed_login_attempts_count >= 0),
        locked_until INTEGER,
        FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    );

- `user_id` is the primary key and references the users 
(in the [Sqlite.Auth.User module](Sqlite.Auth.User)), so there is one password per user.
- `password` is the user's hashed password, stored in PHC string format.
- Both `created_at` and `updated_at` are posix timestamp values. 
- `last_used` is a posix timestamp of the last successful check, or null if never.
- `failed_login_attempts_count` counts consecutive failed checks.
- `locked_until` is the posix timestamp the password stays locked until after too 
many failures, or null when unlocked.

### Password reset tokens table

In addition to the passwords table, this module also owns a table for 
password reset tokens.

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS password_reset_tokens (
        reset_token TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
        user_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
        created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    );

- `reset_token` is the primary key and stores the SHA-256 hash of the token.
- `user_id` references the users and is `UNIQUE`, so there is at most one live
reset token per user.
- `created_at` is a posix timestamp, and `expires_at` is the posix timestamp 
the token stops being redeemable.

unions.name: HashError
unions.comment: Errors that can happen while deriving a password hash.

unions.name: Hashed
unions.comment: A password that has been hashed and is safe to persist.

unions.name: Outcome
unions.comment:
The outcome of validating a candidate password. An expected negative answer
is a value here, not an error.

`Verified` carries the verification
[`Sqlite.Auth.Session.issue`](Sqlite.Auth.Session#issue) requires to issue a
session. `Rejected` means the candidate did not match or the user has no password. 
`Locked` means the password is temporarily locked after repeated failures.

unions.name: Password
unions.comment:
A password, with a phantom type state of either [`PlainText`](#PlainText) or
[`Hashed`](#Hashed). Only the hashed form can be saved to the database.

unions.name: PlainText
unions.comment: A password in plain text, as received from the user.

unions.name: ResetError
unions.comment:
The ways redeeming a reset token can go wrong. 

- `InvalidResetToken` is a token that matches no live row, whether it is unknown, 
already used, replaced, or expired. The caller cannot tell which, deliberately.
- `ResetStorageError` is a database fault.

unions.name: ValidateError
unions.comment:
A real fault while validating: a database error, or a corrupt stored hash
that cannot be verified against.

unions.name: VerifyError
unions.comment:
The ways a stored PHC string can fail to verify against other than a plain
mismatch.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
The options the password functions take.

`iterations` is the PBKDF2 round count for new hashes. The same count is used
for the work [`validate`](#validate) does on a failed check, so pass the same
options to both. Otherwise that work takes a different amount of time than a
real check and the timing gives the difference away.

`maxFailedAttempts` and `lockoutDurationMillis` control the lockout, and
`resetTokenLifetimeMillis` is how long an emailed reset token stays redeemable.
aliases.type: { iterations : Basics.Int, maxFailedAttempts : Basics.Int, lockoutDurationMillis : Basics.Int, resetTokenLifetimeMillis : Basics.Int }

values.name: add
values.comment:
Store a hashed password for the given user, returning the
[`User`](Sqlite.Auth.User#User) on success.

    User.new database secureContext
        |> Task.andThen (Username.new database { username = "alice" })
        |> Task.andThen (Password.add database hashedPassword)
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Sqlite.Auth.Password.Password Sqlite.Auth.Password.Hashed -> Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User

values.name: change
values.comment:
Replace a user's password. This requires the `Verified` type. A password 
check with [`validate`](#validate) creates it, and so does verifying a live session
through [`Sqlite.Auth.Session.verify`](Sqlite.Auth.Session#verify).
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Sqlite.Auth.Password.Password Sqlite.Auth.Password.Hashed -> Sqlite.Auth.Internal.Verified -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error Sqlite.Auth.Internal.Verified

values.name: defaultOptions
values.comment:
The default, recommended, options for password hashing.

    { iterations = 600000
    , maxFailedAttempts = 5
    , lockoutDurationMillis = 15 * 60 * 1000
    , resetTokenLifetimeMillis = 30 * 60 * 1000
    }
values.type: Sqlite.Auth.Password.Options

values.name: fromString
values.comment:
Turn a `String` into a plain-text [`Password`](#Password), ready to
[`hash`](#hash), or to pass to [`validate`](#validate) as the candidate to
check.
values.type: String.String -> Sqlite.Auth.Password.Password Sqlite.Auth.Password.PlainText

values.name: hash
values.comment:
Hash a plain-text password into a [`Password Hashed`](#Password) ready for
[`add`](#add). Uses PBKDF2-SHA256 with `options.iterations` rounds and a random
16-byte salt, and stores the result in PHC string in the database.
values.type: Crypto.SecureContext -> Sqlite.Auth.Password.Options -> Sqlite.Auth.Password.Password Sqlite.Auth.Password.PlainText -> Task.Task Sqlite.Auth.Password.HashError (Sqlite.Auth.Password.Password Sqlite.Auth.Password.Hashed)

values.name: requestReset
values.comment:
Phase one of a forgotten-password reset. Creates a reset token for the given
user and returns `{ token }` exactly once. It's intended for this token to be transmitted
safely, such as being emailed to a user with a known and confirmed email address. 

Phase two is [`reset`](#reset) with the generated token.
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Crypto.SecureContext -> Sqlite.Auth.Password.Options -> Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error { token : String.String }

values.name: reset
values.comment:
Phase two of a forgotten-password reset. Use the generated reset token to set a 
new password. No user is needed, because the token resolves the user itself.

If successful, this function deletes the token, replaces the password, and revokes
all sessions the user may have. This function returns `Verified`, allowing you to
issue a new session if you choose after a successful reset.

    Password.reset database secureContext
        { token = tokenFromLink, new = hashedNew }
        |> Task.andThen (Session.issue database secureContext sessionOptions)
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Crypto.SecureContext -> { token : String.String, new : Sqlite.Auth.Password.Password Sqlite.Auth.Password.Hashed } -> Task.Task Sqlite.Auth.Password.ResetError Sqlite.Auth.Internal.Verified

values.name: validate
values.comment:
Check a plain-text candidate against a user's stored password. This is the
step that gates session issuance. The user argument is the `Maybe` that
[`Sqlite.Auth.Username.user`](Sqlite.Auth.Username#user) returns to make chaining
easier. For example, you might handle user login like this:

    Username.user database { username = candidateName }
        |> Task.andThen (Password.validate database secureContext options candidate)
        |> Task.andThen
            (\outcome ->
                when outcome is
                    Password.Verified proof ->
                        Session.issue database secureContext sessionOptions proof
                    ...
            )
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Crypto.SecureContext -> Sqlite.Auth.Password.Options -> Sqlite.Auth.Password.Password Sqlite.Auth.Password.PlainText -> Maybe.Maybe Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User -> Task.Task Sqlite.Auth.Password.ValidateError Sqlite.Auth.Password.Outcome

Sqlite.Auth.Session.name: Sqlite.Auth.Session
Sqlite.Auth.Session.comment:
Issue, verify, and revoke users' login sessions.

A session is a login token tied to a user. The raw token is handed to the
client once, when the session is issued. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored, so a
stolen database cannot be replayed as live sessions.

## Expected database schema

The minimum required table schema for this module to work is below:

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
        session_token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        last_used_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
        revoked_at INTEGER,
        FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    );

- `session_token` is the primary key and stores the SHA-256 hash of the token,
never the raw token.
- `user_id` references the users (in the [Sqlite.Auth.User module](Sqlite.Auth.User)).
- `created_at` is a posix timestamp, and `expires_at` is the posix timestamp the
session stops being valid.
- `last_used_at` is a posix timestamp of the last successful verification, used
to enforce the idle timeout.
- `revoked_at` is the posix timestamp the session was revoked, or null while live.

unions.name: VerifyError
unions.comment:
Why a presented token failed to verify. `StorageError` is a real database
fault; the rest are expected rejections — the token names no live session.

  - `TokenNotFound` — the token matches no session row at all.
  - `Revoked` — the session was revoked.
  - `Expired` — the session is past its absolute lifetime.
  - `IdleTimeout` — the session went unused for longer than `idleTimeoutMillis`.

aliases.name: Options
aliases.comment:
Options for sessions. `lifetimeMillis` caps a session's absolute age; 
`idleTimeoutMillis` caps how long it survives without being used. A stolen 
token on an abandoned session should not stay live for the rest of the absolute 
lifetime.

aliases.name: Session
aliases.comment:
A row from the `sessions` table. `sessionToken` is the SHA-256 hash of
the raw token, never the raw token itself. `revokedAt` is `Nothing` for a live
session and `Just` the revocation time once it has been explicitly revoked.
aliases.type: { sessionToken : String.String, userId : String.String, createdAt : Basics.Int, expiresAt : Basics.Int, lastUsedAt : Basics.Int, revokedAt : Maybe.Maybe Basics.Int }

values.name: defaultOptions
values.comment:
The default, recommended, options for sessions: a 30-day lifetime and a
7-day idle timeout.

    { lifetimeMillis = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
    , idleTimeoutMillis = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
    }

Pass as-is, or override individual fields:

    { Session.defaultOptions | lifetimeMillis = 60 * 60 * 1000 }
values.type: Sqlite.Auth.Session.Options

values.name: issue
values.comment:
Issue a session for a verified user, the final step of a login pipeline.
This requires the `Verified` type, which a credential check such as
[`Sqlite.Auth.Password.validate`](Sqlite.Auth.Password#validate) produces, so a
session can never be issued for a user who merely exists.

Returns `{ session, token }`. Hand `token` to the client exactly once; it is a
base64 string. Only the token's hash is stored in the database.

    Username.user database { username = candidateName }
        |> Task.andThen (Password.validate database secureContext options candidate)
        |> Task.andThen
            (\outcome ->
                when outcome is
                    Password.Verified proof ->
                        Session.issue database secureContext sessionOptions proof
                    ...
            )
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Crypto.SecureContext -> Sqlite.Auth.Session.Options -> Sqlite.Auth.Internal.Verified -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error { session : Sqlite.Auth.Session.Session, token : String.String }

values.name: migrationV1
values.comment:
Migrate the database to add a `sessions` table with the minimum
required schema for this module to operate. It references users, so run this
after [`Sqlite.Auth.User.migrationV1`](Sqlite.Auth.User#migrationV1).

This migration is meant to be plug-and-play with the `gren-sqlite-migrate`
package. If you are using a different method of migration, the individual SQL
statements can be extracted from the records `statements` field.
values.type: { name : String.String, statements : Array.Array String.String }

values.name: revoke
values.comment:
Revoke a session by its presented raw token. If the given token does
not exist, the `Task` will succeed, but no changes will be made to the
database.
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Crypto.SecureContext -> Sqlite.Auth.Session.Options -> { token : String.String } -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error {}

values.name: revokeAll
values.comment:
Revoke every live session a user holds. This is also the step 
[`Sqlite.Auth.Password.change`](Sqlite.Auth.Password#change) and
[`Sqlite.Auth.Password.reset`](Sqlite.Auth.Password#reset) run, so a stolen
session never survives a credential change.
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> { userId : String.String } -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error {}

values.name: verify
values.comment:
Verify a presented raw token, succeeding with the [`Session`](#Session) it
names together with the `Verified` witness for its user. A successful
verification bumps the session's `last_used_at` to now, and the returned session
reflects it. Anything that makes the token unusable — a revoked, expired, or
idle session, or a token matching no session at all — fails the task with the
matching [`VerifyError`](#VerifyError).

The `verified` field lets a live session authorize actions that require
`Verified` without re-checking a credential:

    Session.verify database secureContext options { token = token }
        |> Task.andThen
            (\{ verified } ->
                Username.change database { newUsername = new } verified
            )

This trades "credential proven just now" for "holds a live session": a stolen
token can reach every action `Verified` gates, including
[`Sqlite.Auth.Password.change`](Sqlite.Auth.Password#change). Require the
stricter proof from
[`Sqlite.Auth.Password.validate`](Sqlite.Auth.Password#validate) where that is
not acceptable.
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Crypto.SecureContext -> Sqlite.Auth.Session.Options -> { token : String.String } -> Task.Task Sqlite.Auth.Session.VerifyError { session : Sqlite.Auth.Session.Session, verified : Sqlite.Auth.Internal.Verified }

Sqlite.Auth.User.name: Sqlite.Auth.User

values.name: get
values.comment:
Look up a user by id, returning the [`User`](#User) for the row. The 
task fails when there's no user with the given id.
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> { id : String.String } -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User

values.name: id
values.comment: Get the id of the given [`User`](#User) as a `String`.
values.type: Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User -> String.String

values.comment:
Migrate the database to add a `users` table with the minimum required

This migration is meant to be plug-and-play with the `gren-sqlite-migrate` 
package. If you are using a different method of migration, the individual 
SQL statements can be extracted from the records `statements` field.
values.type: { name : String.String, statements : Array.Array String.String }

values.name: new
values.comment:
Create a new user with a randomly generated UUID v4 identifier.

This function returns a `User` type which is required for many other 
functions in this package to operate.

It's _highly_ recommended that you immediately create a 
[username](Sqlite.Auth.Username) for the new user in the same SQLite
transaction. After a user is created, the only method of retrieving
it from the database is by it's id (via the [get](#get) function) or by
the users created username. If you plan on using this package for user-facing 
authentication, user ids are not the most friendly way to remember how
to log into an account!
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> Crypto.SecureContext -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User

Sqlite.Auth.Username.name: Sqlite.Auth.Username

unions.name: Normalized
unions.comment: A normalized username that is ready to be saved to the database.

unions.name: Username
unions.comment: A username, with a phantom type state of either `Raw` or `Normalized`.

values.name: change
values.comment:
Change a users username. The user whos username will be changed depends
on the given `Verified` type.

You can obtain the `Verified` type by using any functions in this package that 
verify credentials. This restriction forces callers of this function to go
through the process of properly verifying who a user is before being able to
complete actions on their behalf.

At the time of writing, the only function that can produce the `Verified` type
is the [`Sqlite.Auth.Password.validate`](Sqlite.Auth.Password#validate) function.
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> { newUsername : Sqlite.Auth.Username.Username Sqlite.Auth.Username.Normalized } -> Sqlite.Auth.Internal.Verified -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error Sqlite.Auth.Internal.Verified

values.name: fromString
values.comment:
Turn a `String` into a raw [`Username`](#Username), ready to
[`normalize`](#normalize).
values.type: String.String -> Sqlite.Auth.Username.Username Sqlite.Auth.Username.Raw

values.name: new
values.comment:
Add a username to the given user, returning the user for further pipeline 
steps. The passed username must be normalized using the 
[`normalize`](#normalize) function.
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> { username : Sqlite.Auth.Username.Username Sqlite.Auth.Username.Normalized } -> Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User

values.name: normalize
values.comment:
Ensures the users has has been trimmed, is not empty, and all characters 
are lowercase. This function does not remove empty spaces.
values.type: Sqlite.Auth.Username.Username Sqlite.Auth.Username.Raw -> Maybe.Maybe (Sqlite.Auth.Username.Username Sqlite.Auth.Username.Normalized)

values.name: toString
values.comment: Get the underlying username `String`.
values.type: Sqlite.Auth.Username.Username state -> String.String

values.name: user
values.comment:
Get the user who owns the given username. Returns `Nothing` is the given
username is not associated with any user.
values.type: Sqlite.Database -> { username : Sqlite.Auth.Username.Username Sqlite.Auth.Username.Normalized } -> Task.Task Sqlite.Error (Maybe.Maybe Sqlite.Auth.Internal.User)
